title: Two armed soldiers: God's armor versus the devil's armor
english: On the same psalm: “Sinners have bent their bow” (Psalm 37:14 (Hebrew 37:14; LXX 36:14)). Here are two armed soldiers: the soldier of God wears the breastplate of righteousness, and the soldier of the devil wears the breastplate of unrighteousness; the helmet of salvation stands against the helmet of destruction.
translator_notes: Copy-text PG 12 (Migne) Rufinus Latin via Archive PDF pdftotext; no first-edition GCS.
True OET: no ANF; do not copy Trigg FOTC / Prinzivalli SC / Perrone 2015.
After tip fceb7cfd; Psalms Rufinus Homilia III in Ps 36 CLOSEOUT.
orientation: Origen is beginning a new homily on the same psalm, taking up the verse about sinners bending the bow and contrasting the equipment of God's soldier with that of the devil's soldier.

title: Infants bear neither armor until they can sin
english: Infants bear neither the arms of God nor the arms of the devil until they are able to sin. Glory to God. Amen.
